coverage.focus: Osmosis as water movement across a selectively permeable membrane, then applying that idea to predict what happens to a cell.
essentialIdeas: Osmosis is the movement of water across a selectively permeable membrane from higher water concentration to lower water concentration.
If the water concentration is higher outside a cell than inside, water moves into the cell and it gains water; if higher inside, water moves out and it loses water.
completionEvidence: Learner explains osmosis in their own words after the model.
Learner applies osmosis to predict water movement and the cell effect.
Learner corrects a named gap and reexplains both ideas independently.

methodBriefing.name: Feynman Technique
methodBriefing.what: Study an accurate model, explain it in plain language, repair the comparison, and explain it again without copying.
methodBriefing.why: Putting the idea into your own words reveals gaps and strengthens the mental model.
how: Close it and explain the idea from memory.
Compare your explanation with the model and fix the missing piece.
Explain it again more clearly and directly.
methodBriefing.completion: You can explain osmosis and use it to predict what happens to a cell without relying on the model.
personalization: Use the current task as the starting point.
Keep each answer short and concrete.
Focus on the exact water movement and cell effect.

activities.label: What osmosis is
activities.title: Osmosis and water movement
activities.body: Review the model, then move to the first check.

essentialIdeas: Osmosis is the movement of water across a selectively permeable membrane from higher water concentration to lower water concentration.

activities.label: Explain osmosis
activities.title: Osmosis in your own words
activities.body: Say what osmosis is from memory. Then compare your answer with the model.
activities.correctAnswer: Water moves across a selectively permeable membrane from higher water concentration to lower water concentration.
activities.feedback: A complete answer names water, the membrane, and the direction of movement. If missing, repair the direction or membrane part.

activities.label: Fix the osmosis rule
activities.title: Repair the water movement rule
activities.body: Correct your answer using the model. Give one revised sentence.
activities.misconceptionSummary: Water moves by osmosis without needing a membrane, or water can move in any direction.
activities.correctAnswer: Water moves across a selectively permeable membrane from higher water concentration to lower water concentration.
activities.feedback: The fix is to keep the membrane and the one-way direction of water movement. Do not describe osmosis as any water movement anywhere.

activities.label: Predict cell changes
activities.title: What happens to a cell
activities.body: Choose the best prediction for the cell. Use the model you just repaired.
activities.concept: Use osmosis to predict what happens to a cell
choices: If water concentration is higher outside the cell, water moves into the cell and it gains water.
If water concentration is higher outside the cell, water moves out of the cell and it loses water.
Water always moves out of the cell by osmosis.
The cell changes only if solute moves across the membrane.
activities.correctAnswer: If water concentration is higher outside the cell, water moves into the cell and it gains water.
activities.feedback: Osmosis predicts water movement by comparing water concentration on each side of the membrane. The cell gains water when water moves in.

coverage.focus: Build a first model of osmosis, then use it to predict what happens to a cell.
essentialIdeas: Osmosis is the movement of water across a selectively permeable membrane from higher water concentration to lower water concentration.
If the water concentration is higher outside a cell than inside, water moves into the cell; if it is higher inside, water moves out.
completionEvidence: The learner explains osmosis in their own words.
The learner predicts water movement for a cell case and states the effect on the cell.

methodBriefing.name: Feynman Technique
methodBriefing.what: Study a correct model, explain it in your own words, repair any gap, and explain it again.
methodBriefing.why: Explaining from memory reveals what you understand and what still needs repair.
how: Close it and answer from memory.
Use the feedback to fix only the specific gap.
Explain again without copying the model.
methodBriefing.completion: You have given one explanation, repaired it, and given a second explanation that keeps the core relationship correct.
personalization: Start with the model because this is a novice session.
Keep the repair small and specific.
Use plain language and one simple cell case.

activities.label: Model osmosis
activities.title: What osmosis means
activities.body: Read the model and note the key relationship. Then close it and prepare to explain it back.

essentialIdeas: Osmosis is the movement of water across a selectively permeable membrane from higher water concentration to lower water concentration.

activities.label: Explain the idea
activities.title: Explain osmosis in your words
activities.body: In one or two sentences, explain what osmosis is. Then compare your answer with the model.
activities.correctAnswer: Osmosis is the movement of water across a selectively permeable membrane from higher water concentration to lower water concentration.
activities.feedback: A complete answer names water, the membrane, and the direction from higher water concentration to lower water concentration. If it talks about solute moving, repair that part.

activities.label: Repair the explanation
activities.title: Fix the water movement rule
activities.body: Revise your answer using the feedback. Keep it to one clear sentence.
activities.misconceptionSummary: Confusing water movement with solute movement or leaving out the membrane direction rule.
activities.correctAnswer: Water moves across a selectively permeable membrane from higher water concentration to lower water concentration.
activities.feedback: The repair must keep water as the moving substance and keep the direction rule. Do not switch to solute movement.

activities.label: Model prediction
activities.title: Predict what a cell does
activities.body: Read the example rule and prepare to apply it. Then answer from memory.

essentialIdeas: If the water concentration is higher outside a cell than inside, water moves into the cell; if it is higher inside, water moves out.

activities.label: Apply osmosis
activities.title: What happens to the cell?
activities.body: Choose the best answer for the cell case. Then say why.
activities.concept: Use osmosis to predict what happens to a cell
choices: Water moves into the cell because the water concentration is higher outside.
Water moves out of the cell because the water concentration is higher outside.
Nothing changes because water cannot cross the membrane.
Only solute moves into the cell.
activities.correctAnswer: Water moves into the cell because the water concentration is higher outside.
activities.feedback: Water moves from higher water concentration to lower water concentration. In this case, that means into the cell, which can make the cell gain water.

activities.label: Re-explain the prediction
activities.title: Explain the cell change
activities.body: Explain the water movement and the cell effect in one short response.
activities.concept: Use osmosis to predict what happens to a cell
activities.correctAnswer: If water concentration is higher outside the cell, water moves into the cell and the cell gains water.
activities.feedback: A complete answer links the outside and inside water concentration to the direction of movement and the effect on the cell.
